reply_text:
Agreed: per-problem readiness is for finishing problems that are nearly done, and the DAG should also rank whole areas by how many problems they serve, across both loops. I'll check what area tags already exist before building anything.Both loops are back up on the new ranking. One thing to rule out: I copied `build_step.bb` from a scratch snapshot, so I need to confirm I didn't overwrite anyone else's change to it.㊥ ("theoretical areas (ConstructionTargets) of maximum impact across problems") The DAG now ranks whole theory areas by how many open problems they serve, across both loops, in `71198cf5`. Strategy checkpoints fill most of their slots from that ranking. Per-problem readiness now gets at most one closure row per checkpoint, so a single problem can't absorb every lemma. Both loops restarted on it at about 16:50.

㊢ (how it works)
- **Where areas come from:** an area is either a shared tag from the problem tables in `TOPOLOGY-ROUTES.md`, which already tag all 71 problems, or a lemma's own `:area`. A banked lemma without a tag falls under the ConstructionTargets module its commit wrote.
- **`build_step.bb areas`** (also printed at the end of `priorities`) lists each area with the open registered problems it serves (including the other loop's and unassigned ones), its banked and backlog lemmas, and its modules.
- **Lemma ranking:** among lemmas that are ready to build, the one in the wider area now comes first. Lemmas take `:area` from receipts, and the first spelling is kept.
- **Strategy prompt:** at most one closure-directed row per checkpoint. The other slots go to the highest-impact areas that serve at least one of the loop's own problems, with each area's results built once, in one ConstructionTargets module. Untagged lemmas get tagged as they come up; right now most of the backlog is untagged, so area counts will fill in over the next few checkpoints.

㊬ (checked) Tagging through `add-lemmas` validates and shows up in `areas`. Both live ledgers validate, the lab tests pass, and nobody else had edited the files I replaced.

🈳 (wide areas outside both loops) The widest areas belong mostly to problems neither loop is allowed to work on. **surface-classification** serves 7 open problems (t00A02, t00A03, t91J05, t92J05, t94J04, t96A01, t97J02), and **mayer-vietoris-open-cover** serves 5. All 7 surface-classification problems and most of the Mayer–Vietoris ones are on the unassigned HEAVY list. Election rule 1 limits each loop to its own problem list, so the loops can see these areas but won't build them. Should a loop be assigned areas, such as surface classification, rather than only a fixed list of problems?

previous_reply_acts.text:
(what changed)
- **`priorities` leads with problems.** It now starts with one line per open problem: placeholders, banked lemmas, and backlog lemmas still needed. A problem with no backlog left gets marked `COMPLETE-elect-closure-adapter-now`.
- **Strategy prompt:** a problem whose route is complete gets its closure adapter elected before any lemma. Between closures, the checkpoint steers toward the problem with the fewest backlog lemmas left. Before this, the ranking had no notion of finishing a problem; it only counted how many problems a lemma touched.
